items.title: A defensive call can no longer rewrite the offense
items.premise: The four player-facing tactics share passLeanDelta and aggressionDelta. The simulator consumes those same fields on offensive run/pass choice, offensive fourth-down aggression, defensive coverage, defensive sack rate, and defensive power. Dynamic proof on seed 49008: blitz-heavy writes passLeanDelta -0.05 and aggressionDelta +0.20; prevent writes -0.10 and -0.15, so both defensive calls alter the controlled offense. Object.assign also overwrites the source-derived weekly matchup deltas instead of layering a unit-scoped override.
evidence: src/runtime/advanceWeekCommand.js:9-13
Dynamic in-process capture: run-heavy {-0.15,+0.05}; pass-heavy {+0.15,+0.05}; blitz-heavy {-0.05,+0.20}; prevent {-0.10,-0.15}
items.constraint: The opponent-derived base weekly plan intentionally carries one strategic aggression delta across both units. The repair must preserve that base behavior, add unit-scoped player overrides, restore the original plan after simulation failure, and keep snapshots deterministic.

L1.recipe: Remove passLeanDelta from defensive tactics and stop using their aggression value on offensive call sites.

L2.recipe: Make tacticalFilmRoom the one tactic-definition authority, label every tactic offense/defense, and expose unit-scoped modifiers. Layer offenseAggressionDelta or defenseAggressionDelta over the opponent-derived base plan rather than overwriting it. Route every simulator consumer through a pure unit resolver; add command-seam and engine semantic-isolation tests proving defensive calls cannot alter offensive pass lean/fourth-down aggression and offensive calls cannot alter defensive pressure/power. Surface the unit in film and command receipts.

L3.recipe: L2 plus a two-slot gameplan matrix that lets the player declare both an offensive identity and defensive shell in one bounded weekly command.

items.executionEvidence: Shipped one frozen tactic-definition authority with offense/defense units and layered modifiers; every simulator consumer now resolves the correct unit while preserving the opponent-derived base plan. Command-seam and focused tests prove cross-unit isolation, restoration on failure, deterministic receipts, and versioned tactic authority.

items.title: Repetition becomes deliberate identity instead of modal tax
items.premise: Every regular-season advance unconditionally opens tactic collection and the full Architect red-team modal, even when the player is reinforcing the same executed plan and no source-derived counter-signal changed. This is a structural pacing risk, not a claimed retention outcome. The tactical film ledger already provides an authoritative last executed tactic, so no new hidden state is required.
evidence: public/app.js:358-377 unconditionally wires collectTactic and reviewPlan
public/lib/weeklyPlanComposer.js:64-106 requires the same review loop every regular-season week
public/lib/tacticalFilmRoom.js already publishes bounded recent executed-tactic receipts
items.constraint: Skipping ceremony must never skip a real decision. A new GM choice, failed matching film, owner ultimatum, pending Architect thesis, material adaptation signal, explicit plan change, or first plan must still require full review.

L1.recipe: Preselect the most recent executed tactic in the modal and relabel confirmation as Reinforce.

L2.recipe: Derive a standing plan from the latest bounded tactical-film receipt, preselect it in the browser UI, and add a pure red-flag assessor over live dashboard evidence. A same-plan reinforcement with no material counter-signal commits after one explicit click and emits an honest standing-reinforcement receipt; any first/change/decision/failed-film/ultimatum/thesis/adaptation case opens the full red-team rehearsal. Test composition order, source reasons, UI preselection, and non-mutation on defer.

L3.recipe: L2 plus user-authored persistence rules such as reinforce until opponent soft-side changes or owner pressure crosses a named band.

items.executionEvidence: Shipped a live-evidence standing-plan assessor, visible preselection, one-click Reinforce path, and exact standing-reinforcement receipt. First plans, changes, failed film, GM calls, owner pressure, thesis/adaptation signals, and controlled injuries still force the full Architect rehearsal. Focused UI/composition tests are green.

items.title: A long suite proves where it is without process-table forensics
items.premise: npm test delegates to run-test-shard.mjs, which captures each entire shard through spawnSync with no timeout and writes the aggregate receipt only after all five shards finish. The current direct baseline exceeded sixteen minutes with no durable partial receipt; the active sim-contract shard was discoverable only from Win32 process command lines. This is an observability defect, not a test failure.
evidence: scripts/run-test-shard.mjs runShard uses spawnSync with maxBuffer but no timeout
Atomic receipt is written only after every DEFAULT_SHARDS entry succeeds
2026-08-02 baseline: core + runtime consumed about fourteen minutes under host load before sim-contract began; no partial receipt existed
items.constraint: Partial progress can never be read as a green suite. Exit codes and TAP summaries remain authoritative, and timed-out shards must fail explicitly with their captured diagnostic tail.

L1.recipe: Add a bounded per-shard timeout and print start/end timestamps.

L2.recipe: Add a versioned atomic partial receipt before and after every shard, including PID, start/end, elapsed time, parsed TAP totals, exit/signal/timeout, completed list, and current shard. Add a configurable bounded timeout with explicit timeout classification and preserve direct exit codes. Delete the partial receipt only after the final authoritative aggregate receipt is written. Add focused tests for progress transitions, timeout honesty, and no partial-green interpretation.

L3.recipe: L2 plus resumable same-revision shard proofs keyed to the exact source/test manifest.

items.executionEvidence: Shipped versioned atomic .cache/test-progress.json transitions, runner PID, elapsed/TAP summaries, a configurable 20-minute per-shard bound, explicit timeout/failure classification, stale inspection, and a status CLI. The artifact is structurally authoritative:false and is removed only after a successful final receipt. Focused receipt/coverage tests are green.
